name: The Life and Death of Stars
description: How stars are born, shine and die, from the first light in the young universe to supernovae, pulsars and black holes, and the people who worked it out.

checkpoints.name: First light
checkpoints.note: The universe begins and its first stars light up. Over billions of years the Milky Way grows, and from a cloud of gas, our own Sun and the small red star Proxima Centauri are born.

checkpoints.name: Stars in their prime
checkpoints.note: Stars shine for millions to billions of years. A giant such as Betelgeuse burns fast, while the Sun settles into a long, steady life that allows life on Earth.

checkpoints.name: Seeing stars die
checkpoints.note: Astronomers in several lands record a bright 'guest star' in 1054, and Tycho and Kepler watch new stars of 1572 and 1604 blaze up, showing the sky can change.

checkpoints.name: Reading the light
checkpoints.note: Leavitt, Hubble, Payne-Gaposchkin and Chandrasekhar explain distances, galaxies and stellar death, and pulsars, black holes and supernova 1987A prove it.
